reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the existing cap (3% of bill-of-materials value of Products delivered over the entire term) is not tied to 12 months' fees and is plainly below the 6-month floor, and the clause contains no carve-outs, so MSL's Section 15.1 indemnities, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct all sit inside the cap — expressly walk-away territory under the rule, so it fails the fallback on two material terms.

Redline is actionable and directionally right for us as buyer/customer (IBM): it keeps the clause mutual, resets the basis to the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable and US$1,000,000, adds an Excluded Claims sentence covering indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and preserves the preferred point that IBM's payment obligations are outside the cap.

Edit is confined to paragraph b) and leaves the mutual consequential-damages exclusion in a) untouched; the failed 'minimal edit' check (0.759 changed-character ratio) is expected here because the rule requires replacing the cap basis and inserting carve-outs, which cannot be done with a smaller edit.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, states the preferred position and offers the straight 12-months fallback conditioned on carve-outs, and does not overstate the clause's contents.
No double-flagging or misdirection: the finding expressly excludes the IBM-favourable Section 15 remedies limitation and the loan-agreement provision.
